title: Request Orbit: interactive timeline & correlation map for deep drill-down
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, exploratory tracing workspace called 'Request Orbit' that surfaces a request's timeline as a horizontally scrollable spine and an adjacent radial correlation map that shows related correlation IDs, service clusters, and hot spans. Goal: let engineers and SREs quickly identify cross-service causal hotspots, latency contributors, and per-span token/cost signals without leaving the request view. Key interactions include span hover preview cards, span halo highlighting across lanes, correlation ID orbit filtering, and pinned span snapshots for comparison.
acceptance_criteria: Horizontal timeline with per-span swimlanes that supports zoom (ms <-> s) and sequence scrubbing
Radial correlation map that displays up to 200 correlated request hashes and clusters by service, clickable to focus timeline
Span hover cards show span name, service, latency, token delta, estimated token-cost, KV-cache hit indicator, and link to raw trace
Keyboard-first navigation: arrow keys to move between spans, enter to pin, escape to unpin
Prototype validated with 3 engineers and 1 SRE; actionable feedback captured and at most 2 critical UI issues remaining
decisions: Adopt radial layout for correlation overview to maximize visual grouping of services and keep horizontal timeline focused on sequence
Show estimated token-cost per span (derived from token delta * model-cost-rate) but hide exact billing numbers behind permission
Limit radial orbit to 200 correlated items; provide server-side pagination for larger result sets
Use color ramp aligned with console palette for latency tiers and a separate tonal overlay for cost intensity
tradeoffs: Radial map is denser for many correlations but better for quick cluster recognition; tradeoff is potential occlusion on small screens
Displaying token-cost per span adds useful context but risks confusing non-billing users — we hide billing detail by role
Interactive timeline with continuous-zoom is heavier to implement with long traces; we provide level-of-detail sampling at high zoom-out
accessibility_notes: Ensure all span and cluster actions are reachable via keyboard; provide focus ring and ARIA live updates when pinning
Provide reduced-motion alternative for radial animations and allow high-contrast palette setting
Exported CSV of selected spans for audit/compliance use should be WCAG-compatible content
implementation_constraints: Backend must expose an API endpoint returning correlated request snapshots with pre-aggregated token deltas and KV-cache flags
Timeline needs efficient virtualized rendering of spans and a deterministic lane assignment algorithm to avoid reflows on new data
Radial map should be computed server-side for heavy correlation graphs and return cluster IDs to avoid client CPU spikes
